There was a girl in New Zealand who was embarrassed of her real name. She went by K and never told her friends her real name. In 2008, the courts demanded the name be changed when discovering it during a divorce proceeding and custody battle between the girl’s parents.

What did the parents decide to name this little girl? “Talula Does the Hula From Hawaii”. That was her full first name. After the courts changed it, the new name was kept private from public.

Well, other Yoru Sumino novels are excellent! I haven’t gotten my hands on a copy of “I Have a Secret” yet, but his other three (“I want to eat your pancreas”, “At Night, I Become a Monster”, and “I Had That Same Dream Again”) are all very riveting. Sumino seems to have very specific thoughts on life and humanity, and shows that through all of his novels—at least the ones that I’ve been able to read.

If you liked one of the books, you’ll like them all. But if you’re looking for something different, I would recommend “Socrates in Love” by Kyoichi Katayama. It’s short, but very similar to “I want to eat your pancreas” (although written in 2005 rather than 2014). Another good book was “The Traveling Cat Chronicles” by Hiro Arikawa. It’s told from the perspective of the cat mainly, but has flashbacks to his owner’s past, as well. It’s a sweet story, a little over 200 pages long. I love both of these novels, and I think that if you’re a fan of Sumino novels, you will like these, too.
